## Load package

```{r}
# devtools::install_github("scienceverse/metacheck")
library(metacheck)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readxl)
```

# Get current version of metacheck and save info ----

```{r}
module <- "power"
version <- packageVersion("metacheck")
mc_dir <- file.path("metacheck_versions", version)
dir.create(mc_dir, FALSE, TRUE)
session_info_file <- file.path(mc_dir, "sessionInfo.txt")
capture.output(sessionInfo()) |>
  writeLines(session_info_file)
```

# Get module from github ----

```{r}
mod_version <- 4

if (FALSE) {
  branch <- "main"
  url <- sprintf("https://github.com/scienceverse/metacheck/raw/refs/heads/%s/inst/modules/%s.R", branch, module)
  mod_name <- sprintf("%s_v%d.R", module, mod_version)
  dest <- file.path("modules", mod_name)
  download.file(url, dest)
}
```

Load the file `updated_gt.xlsx` containing ground-truth data and prepare
it for validation:

```{r}
#| eval: false
ground_truth <- read_xlsx(
    here("power", "papers", "psychsci", "updated_gt.xlsx")
  ) |> 
  filter(justification == 1) |>
  
  mutate(
    # Combine "power sensitivity" with "sensitivity"
    power_type = replace_values(
      power_type, 
      "power sensitivity" ~ "sensitivity", 
      "a priori" ~ "apriori",
      "post hoc" ~ "posthoc"
      ),
    
    # Remove any mention of within-subject, between-subject or mixed design 
    # when test is ANOVA
    statistical_test = replace_values(
      statistical_test, 
      c("one-way between-subject ANOVA", 
        "one-way within-subject ANOVA", 
        "one-way mixed ANOVA",
        "one-way ANOVA") ~ "1-way ANOVA",
      c("two-way between-subject ANOVA", 
        "two-way within-subject ANOVA", 
        "two-way mixed ANOVA",
        "two-way ANOVA") ~ "2-way ANOVA",
      c("three-way between-subject ANOVA", 
        "three-way within-subject ANOVA", 
        "three-way mixed ANOVA",
        "three-way ANOVA") ~ "3-way ANOVA"
      ),
    
#. Convert any mention of regression to "regression"
    statistical_test = case_when(
      stringr:::str_detect(statistical_test, "regression") ~ "regression", 
      TRUE ~ statistical_test),
    
    # Convert any other test to "other"
    statistical_test = replace_values(
      statistical_test, 
      c("mediation analysis", 
        "Fisher's r-to-z",
        "structural equation model",
        "Wald test",
        "Mann-Whitney U test",
        "linear mixed effect model",
        "mixed effect model",
        "multilevel model") ~ "other",
        "generalized linear model" ~ "regression"
      ),
  
   # Convert some tests to "other"
  effect_size_metric = replace_values(
      effect_size_metric, 
      c("correlation",
        "Cohen's f2", 
        "incidence-rate ratio",
        "percentage ",
        "q",
        "phi coefficient",
        "coefficient",
        "odds ratio",
        "R2") ~ "other"
      ),

software = replace_values(
      software, 
      c("Power Analysis for General ANOVA Designs program for the R Shiny app",
        "Bayes factor design analysis",
        "Declare-Design",
        "jpower",
        "mc_power_med",
        "Mixedpower",
        "semPower") ~ "other"
      )
)|> 
  
  select(
    text,
    paper_id, 
    paragraph_id,
    power_type:software
    ) |>
  
  mutate(
    power = gsub("[^0-9\\.]", "", power),
    power = as.numeric(power),
    power = ifelse(power > 1, power/100, power)
  ) 
```

## Run power module

We first run the module without using the LLM. This means we classify
power analysis according to word match (i.e., llm_use(FALSE)):

```{r}
# Load papers
papers <- readRDS("papers/psychsci/psychsci.RDS")

# Remove "0956797616647519" paper. This article is about researchers' 
# perception of the power of their studies
papers[["0956797616647519"]] <- NULL

llm_use(FALSE)
mod_version <- 4
module <- sprintf("modules/power_v%d.R", mod_version)
mod_output <- module_run(papers, module)
observed_result <- mod_output$table
```

Save the result for efficiency:

```{r}
if (!is.null(observed_result)) {
  no_llm_path <- sprintf("papers/psychsci/no_llm_result_v%d.Rds", mod_version)
  saveRDS(observed_result, no_llm_path)
}
```

2- Classify power analyses and extract information from them using the
LLM option (i.e., llm_use(TRUE) with local Ollama):

```{r eval=FALSE}
# Set to TRUE to use LLM
llm_use(TRUE)
llm_model("groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b")
llm_max_calls(500)

observed <- module_run(papers, module)
```

# Store the results after running the power module:

```{r}
rds_path <- sprintf("metacheck_versions/%s/llm_result_%s_v%d.Rds", 
                    version,
                    llm_model() |> gsub("/", "-", x = _), 
                    mod_version)
observed$paper <- NULL # remove paper
saveRDS(observed, rds_path)
```

- LLM uses types of statistical tests and effect sizes that are not part
  of the prompt
- LLM adds the G\*Power version to the software column

## Validation

```{r}
# install.packages("clue")
library(clue)

cols <- c(
  "power_type",
  "statistical_test",
  "sample_size",
  "alpha_level",
  "power",
  "effect_size_metric",
  "effect_size",
  "software"
)

matched_list <- list()

# Store indices of matches
matched_obs_indices <- list()
matched_gt_indices  <- list()

paper_ids <- intersect(observed$table$paper_id, ground_truth$paper_id)

for (pid in paper_ids) {

  obs_idx <- which(observed$table$paper_id == pid)
  gt_idx  <- which(ground_truth$paper_id == pid)

  obs_sub <- observed$table[obs_idx, ]
  exp_sub <- ground_truth[gt_idx, ]

  n_obs <- nrow(obs_sub)
  n_exp <- nrow(exp_sub)

  sim_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = n_obs, ncol = n_exp)

  for (i in seq_len(n_obs)) {
    for (j in seq_len(n_exp)) {
      matches <- obs_sub[i, cols] == exp_sub[j, cols]
      sim_matrix[i, j] <- sum(matches, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }

  k <- max(n_obs, n_exp)

  sim_padded <- matrix(0, nrow = k, ncol = k)
  sim_padded[1:n_obs, 1:n_exp] <- sim_matrix

  max_val <- max(sim_padded)
  cost_matrix <- max_val - sim_padded

  assignment <- solve_LSAP(cost_matrix)

  assignment <- assignment[1:n_obs]
  valid <- assignment <= n_exp

  # Store global indices of matches
  matched_obs_indices[[as.character(pid)]] <- obs_idx[valid]
  matched_gt_indices[[as.character(pid)]]  <- gt_idx[assignment[valid]]

  # Build matched data (renamed)
  obs_matched <- obs_sub[valid, ]
  exp_matched <- exp_sub[assignment[valid], ]

  names(obs_matched) <- paste0(names(obs_matched), "_observed")
  names(exp_matched) <- paste0(names(exp_matched), "_ground_truth")

  matched <- cbind(obs_matched, exp_matched)

  matched_list[[as.character(pid)]] <- matched
}

# ---- Combine matched ----
final_matched <- do.call(rbind, matched_list)
rownames(final_matched) <- NULL

# ---- Compute unmatched AFTER loop ----

matched_obs_indices <- unlist(matched_obs_indices, use.names = FALSE)
matched_gt_indices  <- unlist(matched_gt_indices,  use.names = FALSE)

all_obs_indices <- seq_len(nrow(observed$table))
all_gt_indices  <- seq_len(nrow(ground_truth))

unmatched_observed <- observed$table[
  setdiff(all_obs_indices, matched_obs_indices),
]

unmatched_ground_truth <- ground_truth[
  setdiff(all_gt_indices, matched_gt_indices),
]

rownames(unmatched_observed) <- NULL
rownames(unmatched_ground_truth) <- NULL

# ---- Inspect ----
head(final_matched)
head(unmatched_observed)
head(unmatched_ground_truth)

cols <- c(
  "power_type",
  "statistical_test",
  "sample_size",
  "alpha_level",
  "power",
  "effect_size_metric",
  "effect_size",
  "software"
)

# Counts that apply to all columns
n_unmatched_gt  <- nrow(unmatched_ground_truth)
n_unmatched_obs <- nrow(unmatched_observed)

results <- data.frame(
  column = cols,
  TP = NA_real_,
  FP = NA_real_,
  FN = NA_real_,
  PPV = NA_real_,
  FNR = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

numeric_cols <- c("sample_size", "alpha_level", "power", "effect_size")

for (i in seq_along(cols)) {

  col <- cols[i]

  obs_col <- final_matched[[paste0(col, "_observed")]]
  gt_col  <- final_matched[[paste0(col, "_ground_truth")]]

  # Treat mutual NAs as matches
  both_na <- is.na(obs_col) & is.na(gt_col)

  # Use numeric comparison with near() for numeric columns
  if (col %in% numeric_cols) {
    obs_num <- as.numeric(obs_col)
    gt_num  <- as.numeric(gt_col)
    equal <- dplyr::near(obs_num, gt_num)
    equal[is.na(equal)] <- FALSE
  } else {
    equal <- obs_col == gt_col
    equal[is.na(equal)] <- FALSE
  }

  equal <- equal | both_na

  TP <- sum(equal)

  mismatches <- sum(!equal)

  # Apply definitions
  FN <- n_unmatched_gt + mismatches
  FP <- n_unmatched_obs + mismatches

  # Metrics
  PPV <- if ((TP + FP) > 0) TP / (TP + FP) else NA
  FNR <- if ((TP + FN) > 0) FN / (TP + FN) else NA

  # Store
  results$TP[i]  <- TP
  results$FP[i]  <- FP
  results$FN[i]  <- FN
  results$PPV[i] <- PPV
  results$FNR[i] <- FNR
}
```

# Validation metrics

The validation metrics in Table 2 are computed per column (e.g.,
`power_type`, `sample_size`, etc.) using three disjoint sets produced by
the matching procedure above:

1.  **Matched pairs** (`final_matched`): each observed extraction
    aligned to its best-matching ground-truth row via the Hungarian
    algorithm.
2.  **Unmatched ground truth** (`unmatched_ground_truth`): real
    power-analysis instances that were never detected.
3.  **Unmatched observed** (`unmatched_observed`): extracted rows that
    do not correspond to any real instance.

For each column, a matched pair is classified as *correct* if the
observed and ground-truth values are equal (using `dplyr::near()` for
numeric columns; mutual `NA`s count as matches). A matched pair where
values differ is a *mismatch*.

The metrics are then defined as:

- **TP** (True Positive): the number of correct values among matched
  pairs.
- **FN** (False Negative): the number of unmatched ground-truth rows +
  the number of mismatches. Unmatched rows contribute one FN per column
  because the entire instance was missed; mismatches contribute one FN
  because the true value was not recovered.
- **FP** (False Positive): the number of unmatched observed rows + the
  number of mismatches. Unmatched rows contribute one FP per column
  because the system asserted values for a non-existent instance;
  mismatches contribute one FP because the system asserted an incorrect
  value.
- **PPV** (Positive Predictive Value / Precision): TP / (TP + FP). Among
  all values the module predicted for this field, how many were correct?
- **FNR** (False Negative Rate): FN / (TP + FN). Among all real values
  that exist, how many did the module fail to recover correctly?

Note that a single mismatch counts as both a FP and a FN: the system
failed to recover the true value (FN) and asserted an incorrect one
(FP). True negatives are not computed because there is no explicit set
of non-power-analysis instances that were correctly ignored.

results

# Calculate percentage of matches

```{r percentage_match}
percentage_match <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cols, function(col) {
  obs_col <- final_matched[[paste0(col, "_observed")]]
  gt_col  <- final_matched[[paste0(col, "_ground_truth")]]
  both_na <- is.na(obs_col) & is.na(gt_col)
  if (col %in% numeric_cols) {
    eq <- dplyr::near(as.numeric(obs_col), as.numeric(gt_col))
    eq[is.na(eq)] <- FALSE
  } else {
    eq <- obs_col == gt_col
    eq[is.na(eq)] <- FALSE
  }
  eq <- eq | both_na
  data.frame(
    column = col,
    n_agree = sum(eq),
    n_matched = length(eq),
    percentage_match = mean(eq) * 100,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
```

```{r}
if (!is.null(results)) {
  saveRDS(percentage_match, here("power","metacheck_versions", "0.0.0.9106", "validation_percentage_match_v4.Rds"))
}
```

# At least 1 thing actually missing

```{r one_thing_misisng}

cols <- c(
  "power_type",
  "statistical_test",
  "sample_size",
  "alpha_level",
  "power",
  "effect_size_metric",
  "effect_size",
  "software"
)

na_accuracy <- data.frame(
  column = cols,
  n_observed_NA = NA_real_,
  n_correct_NA = NA_real_,
  proportion_correct = NA_real_,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (i in seq_along(cols)) {

  col <- cols[i]

  obs_col <- final_matched[[paste0(col, "_observed")]]
  gt_col  <- final_matched[[paste0(col, "_ground_truth")]]

  # Condition: observed is NA
  obs_is_na <- is.na(obs_col)

  n_obs_na <- sum(obs_is_na)

  # Among those, check if ground truth is also NA
  correct_na <- sum(obs_is_na & is.na(gt_col))

  prop <- if (n_obs_na > 0) correct_na / n_obs_na else NA

  na_accuracy$n_observed_NA[i] <- n_obs_na
  na_accuracy$n_correct_NA[i] <- correct_na
  na_accuracy$proportion_correct[i] <- prop
}
```

```{r}
if (!is.null(results)) {
  saveRDS(na_accuracy, here("power","metacheck_versions", "0.0.0.9106", "validation_na_accuracy_v4.Rds"))
}
```

# At least one of the same columns is missing as identifed missing:

```{r}
cols <- c(
  "power_type",
  "statistical_test",
  "sample_size",
  "alpha_level",
  "power",
  "effect_size_metric",
  "effect_size",
  "software"
)

obs_mat <- sapply(cols, function(col) {
  final_matched[[paste0(col, "_observed")]]
})

gt_mat <- sapply(cols, function(col) {
  final_matched[[paste0(col, "_ground_truth")]]
})

# Logical NA matrices
obs_na <- is.na(obs_mat)
gt_na  <- is.na(gt_mat)

# Ground truth rows with any NA
gt_has_na <- apply(gt_na, 1, any)

# Rows where at least one SAME column is NA
correct_detection <- apply(obs_na & gt_na, 1, any)

n_gt_with_na <- sum(gt_has_na)
n_correct <- sum(gt_has_na & correct_detection)

proportion <- n_correct / n_gt_with_na

n_gt_with_na
n_correct
proportion
```

# Improve sentence capture

```{r}
missed_text <- unmatched_ground_truth$text


# Basic tokenization
tokens <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(missed_text, "\\W+")))

# Remove very short tokens
tokens <- tokens[nchar(tokens) > 2]

# Frequency table
term_freq <- sort(table(tokens), decreasing = TRUE)

head(term_freq, 50)

stopwords <- c(
  "the","and","for","with","that","this","from","were","was","are",
  "but","have","has","had","not","all","any","can","may","our","their",
  "using","use","used","also"
)

term_freq <- term_freq[!(names(term_freq) %in% stopwords)]

head(term_freq, 50)

bigrams <- unlist(lapply(missed_text, function(x) {
  words <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(x, "\\W+")))
  words <- words[nchar(words) > 2]
  if (length(words) < 2) return(NULL)
  paste(words[-length(words)], words[-1])
}))

bigram_freq <- sort(table(bigrams), decreasing = TRUE)
head(bigram_freq, 30)

trigrams <- unlist(lapply(missed_text, function(x) {
  words <- tolower(unlist(strsplit(x, "\\W+")))
  words <- words[nchar(words) > 2]
  if (length(words) < 3) return(NULL)
  paste(words[-c(length(words)-1, length(words))],
        words[-c(1, length(words))],
        words[-c(1,2)])
}))
```

1.  What objects we are using After your matching procedure, you have
    three disjoint sets:

Matched pairs (final_matched) Each row is one observed extraction
aligned to the most similar ground-truth row.

Unmatched ground truth (unmatched_ground_truth) Real power-analysis
instances that were never detected at all.

Unmatched observed (unmatched_observed) Extracted rows that do not
correspond to any real instance.

Everything is defined in terms of these three sets.

2.  Unit of evaluation You are evaluating each column separately (e.g.,
    power, sample_size, etc.). So for a given column, you are asking:

Did the system correctly recover the value of this field?

3.  True Positives (TP) A true positive for a column is:

A matched row where the observed value equals the ground-truth value.

In other words:

the system detected a real instance and it extracted this specific field
correctly

So TP counts correct field recoveries among matched pairs.

4.  False Negatives (FN) False negatives capture missed or incorrect
    recovery of real information. There are two distinct mechanisms:

<!-- -->

(A) Completely missed rows These are rows in unmatched_ground_truth.
    Interpretation:

A real power analysis exists, but the system did not detect it at all.

Because the entire row is missing, every column in that row is
considered missed. So each such row contributes one FN to every column.

(B) Incorrect values in matched rows These are matched pairs where:

the observed value does not equal the ground-truth value for that
column.

Interpretation:

The system found the right instance, but extracted the wrong value for
this field.

Combined FN So for each column:

FN = (missed rows) + (incorrect values in matched rows)

5.  False Positives (FP) False positives capture incorrect claims made
    by the module. Again, two mechanisms:

<!-- -->

(A) Spurious rows These are rows in unmatched_observed. Interpretation:

The system predicted a power analysis that does not exist.

Since that row asserts values for all fields, it contributes:

one false positive for every column.

(B) Incorrect values in matched rows The same mismatches used in FN.
    Interpretation:

The module predicted a value for this field, but it is wrong.

So each mismatch is also a false positive.

Combined FP For each column:

FP = (spurious rows) + (incorrect values in matched rows)

6.  Why mismatches count as both FP and FN This is important and often
    non-intuitive. If the true value is, say, power = 0.80, and the
    model predicts 0.70, then:

it failed to recover the true value → false negative it asserted an
incorrect value → false positive

So the same event contributes to both error types.

7.  True Negatives (TN) You do not compute true negatives. Reason:

You do not have an explicit set of “non-power-analysis instances” that
were correctly ignored.

So the denominator of “all possible negatives” is undefined. This is
standard in extraction tasks and means:

precision and recall are meaningful specificity is not

8.  Precision (PPV) For each column:

Among all values the module predicted for this field, how many were
correct?

Formally:

numerator: correct values (TP) denominator: all predicted values (TP +
FP)

9.  False Negative Rate (FNR) For each column:

Among all real values that exist, how many did the module fail to
recover correctly?

Formally:

numerator: FN (missed + wrong) denominator: total real values (TP + FN)
